audit.whatIsWrong: win[6] read Pantheon for the two-item stage, while whys[6], spikes[3] and the entire late paragraph of the same entry say Tahm Kench takes over past two items.
audit.why: The mirror (audits/top/tahmkench__pantheon.json) settles it: that agent's final shape for the pairing is Pantheon 4 / Skill 2 / Tahm Kench 1, with Tahm Kench owning the two-item stage. My side saying Pantheon there contradicts both the mirror and its own prose.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns, and the spikes were built around 'his W devour' — an ability that does not exist.
audit.why: Abyssal Dive (W) is 21/20/19/18/17s; Tongue Lash (Q) 7s at 900 range; Thick Skin (E) 3s; Devour is the R. The mirror already uses these numbers from the other side.
audit.corrected: Abyssal Dive's 21s and Tongue Lash's 7s/900 written into mid and breakdown.cooldowns; Thick Skin named as the grey health throughout.

audit.whatIsWrong: Six strings say 'W devour' or 'his W devour'. Devour is his R. His W is Abyssal Dive, which the matchup never mentions. Separately, four strings call grey health his 'passive'; grey health is Thick Skin (E), and his passive is An Acquired Taste.
audit.why: Riot's kit: An Acquired Taste (P) stacks on champions; Tongue Lash (Q) is the 900-range slow; Abyssal Dive (W, 21s) is the knock-up dive; Thick Skin (E, 3s) is the grey-health shield and heal; Devour (R) is the eat. 'Bait his W devour then W-in' tells the player to wait for a cooldown that is not the one they think, and 'his grey-health passive' means they never learn that Thick Skin is a 3-second ability they can chip through.
audit.corrected: Devour named as R, Abyssal Dive named as the W with its 21s, Thick Skin named as the grey health, An Acquired Taste named as the passive.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing says that his stun ends Aegis Assault, and the page advises 'eat it into your E block'.
audit.why: An Acquired Taste stacks to three and turns Tongue Lash into a stun; Aegis Assault is a channel that hard CC cancels. The mirror states this same interaction from Tahm Kench's side ('use the stun to cancel Aegis Assault — hard CC ends that channel'), so both directions must say it. Advising the player to hold the channel for the stun is advising them to lose it.
audit.corrected: Reversed in early, whys[2], spikes[1], wants.you[1] and wants.foe[1].

edits.before: Tahm Kench is one of the few melee you can just bully early — at level 1 your point-and-click W stun plus Q does real damage before he has any grey health to soak it. Throw the long-range held Q to chip him while he last-hits, and respect only his tongue (Q) — eat it into your E block if you can, since a landed stun lets him slow-walk away from your trades. At 3 with W-stun, empowered-Q, and E up, you have a clean kill window before his W devour and grey-health passive turn every fight into a wash.
edits.after: Tahm Kench is one of the few melee you can just bully early — at level 1 your point-and-click Shield Vault plus Comet Spear does real damage before Thick Skin has banked any grey health. Throw the long-range Comet Spear to chip him while he last-hits. His passive is An Acquired Taste: three stacks turn Tongue Lash into a stun, and that stun cancels Aegis Assault outright, so never be mid-channel at three stacks. At 3 with W-stun and empowered-Q you have a clean kill window before Devour exists.

edits.before: Keep pressing through 4-6: your empowered-Q poke and E directional block let you chip him faster than his grey health regenerates if you trade in short bursts and reset. Do not commit a full combo into a fresh W devour — bait it, then W-in. At 6 your Grand Starfall is worth more as a roam than a 1v1 finisher here, because Kench is tanky enough to survive a solo R; use it to snowball other lanes while you still own the map tempo.
edits.after: Keep pressing through 4-6: empowered Comet Spear chips him faster than Thick Skin converts grey health back, provided you trade in short bursts and reset. Abyssal Dive is his W, 21s at rank 1 — bait it, then W in; do not confuse it with Devour, which is his R. At 6 Grand Starfall is worth more as a roam than a 1v1 finisher, because Kench survives a solo R; snowball other lanes while you own the tempo.

You must have closed the game on your early lead — win lane, take towers, and end before his sustain and map presence make the duel unwinnable.

notes: This entry had Tahm Kench's W and R swapped six times ('bait his W devour', 'before his W devour comes up', 'his W devour out-last your burst'). Devour is his R; his W is Abyssal Dive, a 21-second knock-up dive that the matchup never mentions at all. So the central piece of advice — 'do not commit a full combo into a fresh W devour, bait it then W-in' — has the player tracking the wrong cooldown. Four more strings call grey health his 'passive'; grey health is Thick Skin (E, 3s) and the passive is An Acquired Taste, whose three stacks turn Tongue Lash into a stun. That stun matters because Aegis Assault is a channel: the page told the player to 'eat it into your E block', which is exactly backwards, and the mirror already states the same interaction from Tahm Kench's side.
